bookTitle: Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives (John C. Hull)
generalAssumptions: Market participants face zero transaction costs and identical borrowing and lending risk-free rates.
Short selling is permitted with full use of short sale proceeds.
Arbitrageurs act instantaneously to eliminate any pricing divergence from theoretical no-arbitrage bounds.

facts.statement: An investment asset is an asset held solely for investment purposes by a significant number of investors (e.g., stocks, bonds, gold, silver). A consumption asset is held primarily for consumption or industrial utility (e.g., crude oil, copper, corn). Arbitrage determines exact forward prices for investment assets, but only provides upper bounds for consumption assets.

facts.topic: Short Selling Mechanics and Dividend Obligations
facts.statement: Short selling involves borrowing securities from an existing owner via a broker and selling them in the market. The short seller must pay all dividends and interest distributions to the lender and must maintain margin collateral until replacing the borrowed securities.

facts.topic: No-Arbitrage Forward Price on Investment Assets with No Income
facts.statement: For an investment asset providing no income, the theoretical forward price for a contract maturing at time T is F_0 = S_0 * e^(r*T), where S_0 is the spot price and r is the continuous risk-free rate.

sourceCitation.section: 5.3 Forward Price for an Investment Asset

variables.definition: Current spot price of the underlying asset
Maturity of the forward contract in years

facts.statement: If F_0 > S_0 * e^(r*T), an arbitrageur executes cash-and-carry: borrow S_0 at rate r, buy spot asset, short forward at F_0, locking profit F_0 - S_0*e^(r*T). If F_0 < S_0 * e^(r*T), an arbitrageur executes reverse cash-and-carry: short spot asset, invest proceeds at rate r, buy forward at F_0.

sourceCitation.section: 5.3 Forward Price for an Investment Asset

facts.topic: Forward Price with Known Discrete Cash Income
facts.statement: When an investment asset provides known cash income with present value I during the contract term, the forward price is F_0 = (S_0 - I) * e^(r*T). Income reduces the effective capital tied up in holding the spot asset.

formulaDetails.name: Forward Price with Known Cash Income

variables.definition: Present value of all cash income during contract term

facts.topic: Forward Price with Known Continuous Dividend Yield
facts.statement: When an asset provides a known continuous dividend yield at annual rate q, the forward price is F_0 = S_0 * e^((r - q)*T). The cost of carry equals (r - q). If dividend yield exceeds risk-free rate (q > r), the forward price trades at a discount to spot.

formulaDetails.name: Forward Price with Continuous Dividend Yield

facts.statement: Between 1992 and 1994, government bond trader Joseph Jett at Kidder Peabody exploited a computer system valuation error where forward reconstitution of stripped Treasury bonds was booked at full undiscounted future value on trade date. This created $350 million in fictitious accounting profits, concealing a real $210 million trading loss and forcing parent General Electric to liquidate the firm.

facts.topic: Short Squeezes and Repo Special Rates (Snapshot 5.2)
facts.statement: When market participants heavily short a specific Treasury bond, demand to borrow that issue in repo markets skyrockets, driving its repo rate far below general collateral rates (trading 'on special' or even negative). Short sellers face severe borrowing fees or forced delivery liquidations (short squeeze).
